title: Lesson 28. If — then
description: The condition "if touching…, then…": the hero collects apples

pairs: If the hero touches the apple

questions.prompt: What happens when the hero touches the apple?
options: A sound and the apple jumps elsewhere

questions.prompt: In the "touching" block you must choose your own hero.
Which sprite do we add second?
questions.explain: Or any food or star from the library.

questions.prompt: A computer can make decisions using conditions.
How do you save the game?

learn.intro: A computer can decide like us: if it rains, take an umbrella. Today we teach the game to decide!

slides.text: In life: if it rains, **then** we take an umbrella. If the light is green, **then** we cross. The computer can do this too — the **"if — then"** block.

check.prompt: What does the "if — then" block do?
options: Checks a condition and acts only if it is true
check.explain: If the condition is true — do it.

slides.text: Add a second sprite — an **apple** (or food, a star). Right now the hero passes through it — nothing happens.
Teach the game: **if** the hero touches the apple, **then** the apple disappears.

check.prompt: Without a condition the hero just passes through the apple.
check.explain: The condition teaches the game to react.

slides.text: The apple's program: when the hero touches it — a "pop" sound and the apple jumps elsewhere. An endless hunt!
slides.code:
when green flag clicked
show
go to random position
forever
    if touching "My hero" then
        play sound "pop"
        go to random position

slides.text: Not working? Check that "touching" has your hero selected and that "if" is **inside "forever"**.

check.explain: Then the game checks all the time.
